findings.title: The public edge transformed the accepted policy; the no-transform correction still requires actual public proof
findings.rationale: The observed delivery defect is established, and the source/candidate remediation is acceptable; actual delivery remains unverified. V8 returned HTTP 200 with privacy_response_bytes_mismatch and performed verified guarded rollback. That receipt did not preserve the mismatching body's length/hash/headers, so its cause cannot be reconstructed from v8 alone. The subsequent admitted Web-only diagnosis supplies the missing boundary evidence: direct Web and gateway returned the accepted 12,865-byte d0f72c588f0f014de46a327e34d6b26125ca115bc973b56bbb926cd8519e701d document without scripts or Cloudflare markers; Windows identity/default and WSL public requests returned 13,396 bytes with all three email-obfuscation markers and one script. This supports transformation at the Cloudflare edge; it is not evidence of a stale gateway upstream, and no exact transformed-body diff was retained. The newly admitted exact NGINX location preserves no-store, adds no-transform and returns 404 if the document is absent. Accepted source and snapshot hash equally to 0cdafce3f985f351a0610e46b76df5babbaefa6c40d428a1bf90e093ce586313. Candidate cfd5e58b91a67d2fae4f37759274a34209cd2501082650a49545a60a12642361 passed nginx -t and direct policy equality/header, root, unchanged JS and API-404 checks. The supplied primary Cloudflare documentation identifies no-transform as an email-obfuscation exclusion, but candidate-local results and that documentation do not prove the future public response.
findings.suggested_action: A, selected and inspected: accept this exact source/candidate and v9 preparation for root adjudication, retaining this finding as an actual-delivery gate until normal-TLS public policy bytes and regression/preservation postconditions pass. Effort low; blast limited to the admitted origin/same-API/Web operation; six template lines to maintain; no identified steady-state regression; direct configuration expresses the required edge behavior. B: if actual public proof rejects this header, stop with bounded response metadata and return a concrete alternative such as a documented document-level obfuscation opt-out for renewed source acceptance. Effort/maintenance higher, changes accepted HTML and its evidence, similar serving cost, and requires an explicit new source delta rather than an unreviewed fallback. C: accept HTTP 200 or the transformed body by weakening equality/no-script requirements. Effort zero, but this discards the accepted static-document contract and leaves the demonstrated delivery defect; it is not an acceptable tradeoff. Do not reload the gateway for a 200 body mismatch.

findings.rationale: A low evidence-provenance residual remains, not a material candidate-code or current-operation blocker. The first localhost HttpClient probe timed out after nginx -t and recorded cleanup attempted, without persisting its generated container ID/name or removal exit code. The successful second probe records exact owned container 97a87b708ceaa6698447b3522b25f2aad53e8ff2a28c114de02396a1ef8d35a9 and its removal. This bounds current resource concern but cannot turn the first attempted cleanup into a verified historical action. General wording about owned temporary cleanup must retain that distinction.
findings.suggested_action: A, recommended: retain the explicit historical limitation and the current scoped absence readback, record this low residual honestly, and retain exact identity/removal status in any future temporary-resource receipt. Effort low; no additional mutation blast; small evidence-maintenance cost; no product performance cost; clear provenance without reconstructing missing facts. B: perform another explicitly admitted isolated probe with fully retained identity and cleanup if new candidate behavior requires it. Effort and transient resource cost higher, but even a new successful run cannot prove the first historical cleanup; no such repeat is required by the present candidate evidence. C: infer exact historical cleanup from an attempted removal or current zero-count query. Effort zero but unsupported evidence, weaker operational structure and no compensating performance benefit. Do not broaden cleanup or inspect unrelated resources to erase this qualification.
